item.title: Gilded Capability: Overinvestment and the Survivability Paradox
item.description: Infernos raged aboard Japanese aircraft carriers after U.S. Navy dive-bombers found their marks during the Battle of Midway. Many Japanese pilots were incinerated in ready rooms and in the cockpits of their aircraft while they sat idling on flight decks. Those who were airborne returned to find their carriers aflame. item.title: Running to Stand Still: Russian Nuclear Modernization after New START
item.description: John Maynard Keynes once wrote, “The difficulty lies, not in the new ideas, but in escaping from the old ones”: an apt depiction of the current discourse and debate of what the world will look like now that the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START) treaty has expired. item.title: The Sound of Munich: Autonomy, Anxiety, and the Twilight of Transatlantic Order
item.description: Munich was warmer than Washington this weekend, both in weather and in sentiment. Neither development was widely forecast. item.title: The Greatest Threat to Acquisition Transformation Is Fear
item.description: The Department of Defense’s acquisition and sustainment culture is pathologically risk-averse. It is not congressional oversight, statutory constraints, insufficient training, or an absence of strategy.The greatest threat is fear.
